newsitem.title: SPAIN: DIVING-GERMANY WIN INAUGURAL SYNCHRONISED DIVING TITLES.
newsitem.headline: DIVING-GERMANY WIN INAUGURAL SYNCHRONISED DIVING TITLES.

text.p: Germany won the first two synchronised diving titles in European championship history on Tuesday.
Diving from two adjacent boards Holger Schlepps and Alexander Mesch won the men's synchronised three-metre springboard title by a tiny margin from Spanish pair Jose Luis Hidalgo and Ruben Santos.

But in contrast fellow Germans Ute Wetzig and Anke Piper won the inaugural women's synchronised title on the San Pablo pool's double-width 10-metre highboard by a huge amount from Odile Arboles-Souchon and Julie Danaux of France.

In the men's event, Hidalgo and Santos scored over 10 points more than the Germans on their last dive but, to the disappointment of Spanish fans, it was not quite enough for a first title at these championships for the host nation.
Schlepps and Mesch scored 284.34 points from their five dives, with Hidalgo and Santos second (283.92) and Italy's Nicola Marconi and Donald Miranda third (277.38).
Wetzig and Piper amassed 269.76 points to win the women's title from Arboles-Souchon and Danaux (240.54) and Austrians Marion Reiff and Anja Richter (215.67).
Newly-crowned individual highboard champion Olga Khristoforova had three disappointing dives out of five and she and Russian team mate Evgenia Olshevskaya managed only fourth place out of five.
Marks were awarded for execution -- two marks for each diver -- and synchronisation.
